# hands/story

the story so far, and the studio's desk.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/story <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): beat
- Job (writes state or calls the core): record-run; slot-claim; slot-mark
- Operator only (never call): seed
- Read only: state; due [--days N]; desk [--hours N]; audit [--storyline K]; runs [--limit N] [--full]

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | R | `{storylines: [{key, title, premise, state, open_question, question_at, next, status, updated_at, beats_total, beats: [the last 3, newest first: {id, storyline, at, post_id, surface, format, shape, text, open_question, refs}]}]}`, active ones only, oldest first. |
| `due [--days N]` | R | Active storylines whose open question has waited more than N days (1 to 30, default 3) with no beat since, the longest wait first: `{days, due: [{key, title, open_question, next, question_at, last_beat_at, waiting_days, reason}]}`. |
| `desk [--hours N]` | R | What really happened in the last N hours (1 to 168, default 24), below. |
| `audit [--storyline K]` | R | Every beat's refs resolve, below. |
| `beat` | A | `{storyline, post_id, text, open_question?, shape?, format?, surface? |
| `seed` | O | Inserts each seed storyline the ledger lacks; one already there keeps its live fields (`{added, kept}`). |
| `record-run` | J | One `bin/studio` run record on stdin (`{id, at_unix, outcome: published\|picked\|empty\|vetoed\|skipped\|failed, kind? |
| `runs [--limit N] [--full]` | R | The newest studio runs (10, at most 100), newest first: `{runs: [{id, at, slot, dry, seed, explore, outcome, reason, models: {writer, editor}, pitches, drafts, calls, secs, pick, kind, post_id}]}`; `--full` adds each run's whole `record` (since 2026-11-22: its cards, posts, rank… |
| `slot-claim` | J | `{slot_id, run_id, force?}`: a studio slot's one run (`studio_slots`), claimed by bin/studio before any model turn, under `DRY_RUN` too. |
| `slot-mark` | J | `{slot_id, run_id, status, intent?, post_id?}`: the holding run's progress (`claimed`, `posting` with the draft before hands/x is called, `posted` with the post id, `empty`, `skipped`, `failed`, `in_doubt`); a run that does not hold the slot changes nothing (`{marked: false}`). |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `audit`, `beat`, `desk`, `due`, `record-run`, `runs`, `seed`, `slot-claim`, `slot-mark`, `state`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--days`, `--full`, `--hours`, `--limit`, `--storyline`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `hands/story <verb> --help` (never put a VAR= in front of a command: the shell refuses it, and DRY_RUN is not yours to set). The full account is in docs/hands.md.
